assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into long-acting agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity is a physiology-to-therapy arc of exceptional originality and very large clinical and societal impact. The physiology (insulinotropic action, appetite and gastric effects) is clear and now supported by cardiovascular and renal outcome trials.
assessment.attribution: The credited list spans physiological discovery (Holst, Drucker), identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide form (Mojsov) and drug development (Knudsen, Novo Nordisk). A three-person prize centred on the biology is feasible, but omits Knudsen and, in the wider literature, other early peptide contributors such as Habener who are not in the credited names; this is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent large phase 3 and outcome trials, widespread clinical use, stable mechanistic interpretation. Timely, arguably overdue given impact.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit between GLP-1 identification, the physiological work and pharmaceutical development is contested.
Long-term safety and central-mechanism details of obesity indications are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors to eradicate haematological malignancies created a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with durable remissions in refractory leukaemia and lymphoma. Originality and clinical impact are high.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T translation with costimulatory domains), Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and CAR design) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early clinical proof of principle) form a credible trio. Eshhar and others who contributed first-generation CARs are not in the credited list, which complicates the picture.
assessment.maturity: Mature for haematological cancers with approved products and long follow-up; solid-tumour efficacy remains limited. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept versus clinical optimisation is disputed.
Toxicity (cytokine release, neurotoxicity, secondary malignancy signals) and solid-tumour limits remain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, converting a fatal paediatric neuromuscular disease into a treatable one. It is a clear, original discovery with dramatic benefit and opened a platform for splice-switching therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing regulatory element and target sequence; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development. The pair maps naturally to the discovery and therapeutic halves. Other contributors (e.g. SMN gene discovery by Melki and colleagues, Adrian Krainer's collaborators at Ionis) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with nearly a decade of clinical follow-up; independent replication and subsequent related therapies support the interpretation. Timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should include the SMN1 gene discovery is not resolvable from the supplied credit.
Long-term durability and treatment-timing effects are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling (IRE1/HAC1 and later ATF6/PERK arms) and is fundamental to proteostasis, with relevance to diabetes, cancer and neurodegeneration. Conceptually original and widely confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are widely regarded as the decisive contributors, with Mori's HAC1/UPRE work and Walter's IRE1 and mRNA splicing mechanism. Others such as Kozutsumi and Ron may be raised, but the two-person configuration is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation across species and disease contexts. Recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Direct clinical therapeutic payoff is still emerging, which may weigh against it relative to translational candidates.
I am relying on recalled literature rather than the supplied text for contributor details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity in intact circuits and has transformed experimental neuroscience, with early clinical applications in vision restoration. The impact on a field I know well is substantial and the originality high.
assessment.attribution: Discovery and characterisation of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its application in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden, also Miesenböck's earlier work) makes the six-name list far larger than three. Choosing Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth is one defensible configuration but excludes Bamberg and Boyden.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a tool: thousands of independent studies. Clinical translation is limited and early.
uncertainties: Severe attribution crowding means any three-person prize is contentious.
Primarily a tool rather than a disease-oriented discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and expanded to dystonia and other disorders; I see its clinical impact directly in movement-disorder practice. The invention is clear and durably useful.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the credited single name for the high-frequency stimulation concept and early clinical implementation. Other contributors (e.g. DeLong's basal ganglia circuit work, Limousin, Krack, neurosurgical colleagues) are not in the supplied credited names, which could complicate a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of clinical use and randomized trials. Timely or late.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate award adequately reflects the circuit physiology and clinical development.
Mechanism of DBS action remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of growth and nutrient responses is foundational for cell and metabolic biology and relevant to ageing, cancer and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genes in yeast; Schreiber and Sabatini contributed to mammalian mTOR/FKBP12-rapamycin biochemistry. A single Hall prize or a combination is possible; I prefer the narrowest defensible configuration given unresolved credit and that other credited contributors are limited to those named.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent confirmation, though clinical rapalog benefit outside transplantation and some cancers has been modest.
uncertainties: Contribution of the mammalian mTOR discoverers relative to Hall is debated.
Reputational or conduct issues around some credited individuals should not be assumed from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of alpha-synuclein as the major component of Lewy bodies and tau in neurofibrillary tangles clarified the molecular pathology of Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease and underlies biomarkers such as seed-amplification assays and PET tracers. Foundational, though translational payoff remains incomplete.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert are the principal credited contributors to the filament and Lewy body protein discoveries. Other groups (e.g. Lee, Trojanowski, Kosik, Grundke-Iqbal on tau) are not in the credited names, and Spillantini's work with Goedert on synuclein is the more distinctive part.
assessment.maturity: Mature as pathology and increasingly as biomarker science; disease-modifying therapies based on it are not yet established.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: tau and synuclein may merit different recognition and credit.
No approved therapy yet derived directly from the discovery.
